cards.title: IBM's Granite PatchTST-FM-r2 Claims Top Zero-Shot Forecasting Spot on GIFT-Eval Under Permissive License
cards.why_it_matters: A commercially-licensed, open-weight time-series foundation model hitting SOTA zero-shot benchmarks is directly relevant if you work on forecasting pipelines or production ML infrastructure.
cards.summary: IBM released Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2, a ~385M-parameter time-series foundation model. As of September 8, 2026, it ranks #1 among replicable zero-shot models with permissive licenses (Apache 2.0 / OpenMDW 1.0) on GIFT-Eval, and #2 overall in that zero-shot replicable category. It supports probabilistic forecasting via a 99-quantile head, context lengths up to 8,192, and missing-value imputation. Backbone uses conformer blocks combining multi-head self-attention with temporal convolution.

cards.title: Why Most People Still Don't Feel AI's Impact — And When They Might
cards.why_it_matters: As someone deep in the AI bubble, this essay offers a grounding calibration on the gap between field-level excitement and real-world diffusion that shapes the societal context your work exists within.
cards.summary: Most people's daily touchpoints with AI — image generation, enhanced search — are marginal. Unlike past industrial revolutions that delivered tangible physical goods, AI's near-term benefits (scientific breakthroughs, new therapeutics) risk being too indirect for average people to attribute to AI. The author argues early-stage AI's real value is building compounding foundational infrastructure over decades, not immediate consumer-visible change.

cards.title: IdeaAMBIG Benchmark Reveals LLMs Fail at Locating Implementation Gaps in Research Specs
cards.why_it_matters: This benchmark directly measures whether AI coding agents can faithfully implement research methods from specs — a core bottleneck for AI-assisted research and automated reproducibility pipelines you may work with.
cards.summary: IdeaAMBIG is a 660-instance benchmark testing LLMs on codification-readiness assessment, defect localization, and clarification generation in research method specs. Across 13 LLMs, best defect localization on real-world instances reaches only 9.6% Macro Defect Recovery Rate, while clarification success (given the defect) reaches 80.6%. Oracle experiments show gold resolutions raise codification-ready rate from 14% to 98%, identifying defect localization as the primary bottleneck.

cards.title: Bell-Type Tests Without Bell Tests: Quantum vs. Classical Time Evolution via Correlation Patterns
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers interested in quantum ML or quantum computing foundations, this proposes a new discriminator between quantum and classical dynamics applicable where standard Bell tests cannot be constructed.
cards.summary: The paper explores using statistical correlation patterns as Bell-type tests in settings where standard Bell tests are infeasible (e.g., cosmology). It shows quantum vacuum fluctuations in closed Hamiltonian systems produce time-independent correlations controlled by the energy gap, while classical Hamiltonian systems exhibit apparent poles at physical frequencies leading to time-dependent, eventually dephasing correlations. The approach is extended to quantum optics, quantum walks, and quantum search.

cards.title: Normalizing Flows Automatically Extract Near-Pivotal Statistics Under Nuisance Parameters
cards.why_it_matters: A technically relevant result for researchers doing simulation-based or likelihood-free inference, showing normalizing flows can automate nuisance-robust statistic construction with provable near-pivotality.
cards.summary: The paper presents a normalizing flow decomposition that extracts near-pivotal statistics in the presence of nuisance parameters using only a sample generator. Near-pivotality is defined by minimum average KL-divergence of p-values versus uniform. The method recovers the one-sample t-test almost exactly, outperforms the Welch test on worst-case size, and achieves better power and speed than profile likelihood-ratio techniques on small-to-moderate samples.

cards.title: Noether Symmetries Provide General Route to Deterministic Energy Harvesting from Quantum Sources
cards.why_it_matters: Relevant to quantum thermodynamics foundations underlying quantum computing hardware and quantum information theory — provides a symmetry-based framework for a previously ad hoc phenomenon.
cards.summary: The paper establishes that any continuous symmetry with a conserved Noether charge generates orbits of source states all capable of deterministic energy harvesting (absorbing energy without absorbing entropy), provided harvester boundary states are symmetry-invariant. One DEH-capable state with nonzero charge-sector asymmetry generates infinitely many simultaneous DEH-capable states. Results are illustrated with Jaynes-Cummings, three-spin XX chain, and SU(2) models, and extended to generalised probabilistic theories.

cards.title: Gap-Entropy Conjecture Resolved for Best-Arm Identification in Fixed-Confidence Bandits
cards.why_it_matters: A clean theoretical resolution of a long-standing conjecture in bandit theory — directly relevant to RL researchers and anyone working on sample-efficient exploration or adaptive experiment design.
cards.summary: The paper proves the gap-entropy conjecture for fixed-confidence best-arm identification with independent unit-variance Gaussian arms. The optimal expected sample complexity, averaged over arm-label permutations, is within constant factors of H(log(1/δ) + Ent(I)), where H is the sum of inverse-squared gaps and Ent(I) is an entropy term over gap-magnitude buckets. An instance-independent algorithm achieves this bound up to constants plus a term involving the minimum gap.

cards.title: Finite-Witness Characterization of Language Generation in the Limit, Verified in Lean
cards.why_it_matters: Foundational theory on the limits of generative language models from a learning-theoretic perspective — niche but relevant to researchers thinking rigorously about what LLMs can and cannot learn.
cards.summary: The paper characterizes when language generation in the limit is possible: exactly when each target language can be assigned a finite positive witness such that targets activated by any finite sample share an infinite common intersection. A separation-width hierarchy with multiple distinct levels is established and fully verified in Lean 4, including cases requiring unbounded finite witnesses and cases where no finite-witness assignment exists.
